topics.label: Introduction and Hallmarks of Cancer Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture, outlines the learning outcomes, and establishes the hallmark framework for understanding tumor progression.

topics.label: Growth Factor Signaling and Sustained Proliferation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades, including Wnt and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways, drive uncontrolled proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Leukemias and Carcinomas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how arrests in normal lineage differentiation contribute to neoplastic transformation across both hematopoietic malignancies and solid intestinal tumors.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptotic Cell Death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor cells evade programmed cell death through disruptions in p53 signaling and the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Telomeres, Replicative Immortality, and Stress Integration
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms of cellular senescence and telomerase reactivation that enable replicative immortality, the role of p53 in coordinating these stress responses, and summarize cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming and Oncometabolites in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the metabolic rewiring of tumor cells toward aerobic glycolysis and the role of Krebs cycle mutations and oncometabolites in promoting cancer progression.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the angiogenic switch and the vascular mechanisms tumors require to overcome nutrient and oxygen diffusion limits.

topics.label: Invasion, Circulation, and Metastatic Colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the multistep metastatic cascade, covering invasion pathways, circulating tumor cells, microenvironmental compatibility, and the genomic features of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Conclusion and Lecture Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the overall themes of the lecture and provides concluding remarks on how the hallmarks of cancer integrate across tumor types.
